summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma and recent history of E. coli bacteremia and C. difficile infection, was admitted with high fevers and chills following fiducial marker placement for Cyberknife radiation. He was found to have recurrent E. coli bacteremia with a multidrug-resistant pattern, leading to a diagnosis of sepsis. He was treated with intravenous meropenem and oral vancomycin, the latter continued to prevent C. difficile recurrence. His fevers resolved after two days, and he stabilized with correction of electrolyte imbalances. A PICC line was placed for outpatient administration of ertapenem. His home medications, including atenolol and terazosin, were restarted. He was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics and follow-up planned with oncology for radiation and chemotherapy resumption.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of intrahepatic bile ducts
